findings.claim: The Windows jobs rely on the npm command shim, violating the requirement that no step rely on a .cmd shim.
findings.evidence: specs/continuous-integration/spec.md says: "No step SHALL rely on a `.cmd` shim or on a globally installed CLI." The workflow uses `- run: npm ci`; on `windows-latest` with the default PowerShell shell, `npm` resolves through the installed `npm.cmd` shim.
findings.suggested_fix: Invoke npm through its JavaScript CLI with `node` instead of the `npm` command, or narrow the OpenSpec requirement if the no-shim rule was intended to apply only to the OpenSpec validation step.
